Single thick braid — plaited tight from crown to ends, tied with leather cord, keeps hair secure during long marches and combat.
Two side braids — Dutch-braided close to scalp on each side, practical for helmet wear and prevents tangles on the road.
Long warrior-tail — high ponytail bound multiple times with cord, keeps hair off neck during exertion and away from grabbing hands.
Utility ponytail — low, tight gathering at nape, secured with leather thong, stays put under hoods and through rough travel.
Cropped short — cut bluntly at jaw-length with a belt knife, requires no maintenance, dries quickly after river crossings.
Undercut with top-knot — sides shaved, remaining length twisted into a knot, cool in heat and stays completely secured.
Shaved sides with long top — temples buzzed, center length tied back, reduces weight while maintaining some hair for warmth.
Hooded and hidden — tucked entirely under a deep hood, protected from weather, dust, and identifying features concealed.
Head-scarf wrapped — wound tightly in linen or cotton, desert-style, shields from sun and sand, nothing loose to catch.
Wrapped under hood — coiled at nape beneath a close-fitting coif, hair contained for stealth and protected from brambles.
Pinned under padding — rolled and pinned flat beneath quilted helmet cap, no bulk to interfere with armor fit.
Loose with forehead-band — leather strap keeps hair from eyes, length left free but controlled, quick to arrange each morning.
Cord-wrapped length — hair gathered and spiral-bound with thin rope from root to tip, cannot come undone during movement.
Dreadlocked — matted into thick ropes over months of travel, requires no daily styling, naturally stays out of the way.
Wild and tangled — uncombed and knotted from weeks without care, functional through sheer neglect, no maintenance possible or attempted.
Simple top-knot — twisted and wound into a bun at crown, secured with its own length, classic and practical.
Bone-pin chignon — low bun at nape, held with sharpened bone pins that double as emergency weapons in close quarters.
Partial braid crown — front sections braided back from face, rest gathered in low tail, keeps vision clear without full braiding.
Box-braids — sectioned and tightly braided close to scalp in geometric rows, lasts weeks without re-doing, extremely secure.
Twin ropes pinned up — two thick braids coiled and pinned to crown, compact style that fits under helmets easily.
Wrapped and knotted — length twisted into a rope and knotted repeatedly on itself, creates a short club that won't unravel.
Side-swept and tied — gathered over one shoulder and bound in sections with multiple ties, accessible but controlled for travel.
Braided and coiled — single plait wrapped around head like a crown, secured with wooden pins, nothing hangs loose.
Knotted at nape — simply tied in a basic knot against the neck, crude but effective, takes seconds to secure.
Twisted and pinned — sections twisted back from face and pinned with whatever's available, improvised daily with found items.
